summary: Forest Service lookout at Fort Klamath, Klamath County: 20-ft steel tower built 1958, airlifted to Sugarpine Mountain in 1970. The Fort Klamath site has no tower now.

facts.status_note: Tower airlifted to Sugarpine Mountain in 1970 and now stands there; the Fort Klamath site has no tower.

Tower airlifted to Sugarpine Mountain, Winema National Forest

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register describes the earlier Fort Klamath lookout as a platform above the community center. A 1949 item quoted on the Rex's page calls it the Grange Hall tower. The story reports both descriptions.

The 1948 item in the Rex's page sits under Rogue River National Forest records. The register and Forest Fire Lookout Association list the site under Winema National Forest, and the story uses the current listing.
The register gives 42.70474, -121.99862. The Forest Fire Lookout Association list gives 42.70063, -121.99745. The record keeps the register coordinates.

notes_for_editor: Brief status gone refers to the Fort Klamath site; the tower itself is at Sugarpine Mountain (us-or-sugarpine-mountain may need its own record). height_m 6.1 is 20 ft converted to metres. The register gives 4,200 ft elevation, matching the brief. No access information in any source, so no access key. No photos added: no image URLs were captured. The 1949 Grange Hall reference may describe the same building as the community center platform; the sources do not say so.
